## Tours to Devil's Crown in the Galápagos: which cruise to choose

[Devil's Crown](/ecuador/place/devils-crown/) is the rocky rim of a collapsed volcanic crater near [Floreana Island](/ecuador/place/floreana-island/) in the Galápagos Archipelago. Jagged rock pinnacles rise above the ocean, while underwater reefs support schools of fish, sea turtles, rays and sea lions. Wildlife sightings depend on the conditions of each outing and are a welcome possibility, not a guaranteed checklist.

Our catalog features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} passing through this part of the archipelago. Both current itineraries visit Floreana but differ considerably in length, mainland sightseeing and time available for the other Galápagos Islands.

**The key feature of Devil's Crown is that it is a marine stop without landing on the rocks.** You view it from a boat and may snorkel if conditions permit. Currents and swell mean that the accompanying guide and crew decide whether entering the water is safe. A place name appearing in the itinerary does not imply that scuba diving is included.

## Two ways to experience it

| Itinerary | When Devil's Crown is visited |
|---|---|
| [8-day VIP Galápagos Cruise](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-luxury-yacht-cruise-8-days/) | Floreana Island, day 2 |
| [18-day Ecuador and Galápagos Journey](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/) | Marine segment, day 16 |

**If the islands and the ocean are your priority.** On the [8-day yacht itinerary](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-luxury-yacht-cruise-8-days/), the journey begins on Santa Cruz before the yacht approaches Floreana. Planned stops include Punta Cormorant, Devil's Crown, Post Office Bay and the Baroness Lookout. The cruise then continues to other islands, including Isabela and Fernandina. Choose this option for successive days at sea, island-to-island travel and opportunities to observe marine wildlife.

**If you also want to explore mainland Ecuador.** The [18-day tour](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/) starts with the Andean highlands, Otavalo, protected areas, the Amazon and volcanic scenery. Day 15 includes a flight to the Galápagos and boarding the M/Y Grand Majestic yacht. On day 16, the route reaches Floreana, where Devil's Crown is scheduled after Post Office Bay and Punta Cormorant. The cruise segment lasts 4 days and 3 nights.

The overall duration alone is not the most useful comparison. On the 18-day itinerary, most of the time is devoted to mainland Ecuador; the 8-day cruise focuses entirely on the islands. Travelers interested in marine excursions and underwater wildlife should compare the **number of days aboard the yacht**, not just the length of the whole holiday.

## What happens during the crater stop

Devil's Crown has volcanic origins: the ocean eroded much of the crater, leaving several rocky pinnacles above the water. Floreana and its surrounding waters are part of the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/), where conservation rules affect visits. The guide chooses an authorized viewing location and, in favorable conditions, accompanies guests snorkeling.

Snorkelers appreciate the rich marine life around the rugged rocks. Different fish, turtles, sea lions and rays may be encountered, while seabirds rest on the outcrops. Strong currents, however, present an extra challenge even to confident swimmers. The safe route, whether a life jacket is needed and permission to enter the water are determined on site.

Those interested in marine wildlife and birdwatching can also browse our [Wildlife and Safari](/interests/wildlife/) collection. If a multi-day voyage itself appeals to you, explore [Cruises and Expeditions](/interests/cruises-and-expeditions/) and the full [Ecuador tours catalog](/ecuador/tour/).

## How Devil's Crown differs from other stops on Floreana

At [Punta Cormorant](/ecuador/place/punta-cormorant/), the experience focuses on coastal birds, a lagoon and walking ashore. [Post Office Bay](/ecuador/place/post-office-bay/) is known for the historical tradition of exchanging postcards through a barrel mailbox. Devil's Crown, by contrast, is primarily about volcanic rock formations and life underwater.

These places may be visited on the same day but offer very different experiences. A different cruise listing Floreana does not automatically include Devil's Crown. Before choosing a tour, check the full list of stops and what is planned at each one.

## What to consider before traveling

**Conditions in the water.** Swell and currents near the crater can change. Even experienced swimmers should follow their guide and the operator's requirements. Snorkeling and scuba diving are distinct activities and cannot be treated as interchangeable because they take place at the same natural attraction.

**Travel between islands.** The 8-day itinerary devotes more time to the ocean and islands. On the 18-day journey, the cruise is combined with a full mainland program. Daily schedules, frequency of transfers, climate and packing needs differ between the two parts of the journey.

**Changes to schedules.** Marine routes depend on authorized visitor sites and weather. Confirm the sequence of visits, availability of snorkeling and exact time on the water against your chosen itinerary before departure.

## Frequently asked questions about Devil's Crown tours

### Can you land on the rocks of Devil's Crown?

No. A standard visit to this marine site involves no landing. The rocks are viewed from the boat, with snorkeling possible if conditions allow.

### Which tour spends more time in the Galápagos?

The [8-day VIP cruise](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-luxury-yacht-cruise-8-days/) focuses entirely on the archipelago. On the [18-day journey](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/), the marine segment lasts 4 days and 3 nights, with the remaining days on mainland Ecuador.

### Do you have to be able to swim to visit?

Swimming skills are not required to view the rocks from a boat. If you want to snorkel, assess your ability in the water: the area is known for currents, so participation depends on the conditions and the guide's decision.

### Are sea turtle encounters guaranteed?

No. This is a natural habitat, and the presence and visibility of animals vary. Choose a tour based on its itinerary and time at sea, treating wildlife sightings as part of an authentic natural experience.

## El Ángel Ecological Reserve: the high-altitude páramo of northern Ecuador

El Ángel Ecological Reserve (Reserva Ecológica El Ángel) lies in Carchi Province in northern [Ecuador](/ecuador/), near the Colombian border. This protected Andean highland area combines open grasslands, lagoons, wetlands and patches of Polylepis woodland.

Its most recognizable scenery is the dense stands of **frailejones**, plants with rosettes of long, pale leaves. Rising above grasses and mist, they make a walk through the local páramo very different from an ordinary forest trail. This is not the hot tropical climate often associated with Ecuador: altitude, wind and damp cold shape the experience.

El Ángel protects a natural system that helps supply water to nearby communities. Its soils and highland wetlands retain rainwater and gradually release it into streams. Exploring this landscape reveals how the Andes' natural watersheds function.

## Frailejones: the plants that draw visitors to El Ángel

Frailejones are characteristic of the high elevations of the northern Andes. Their leaves are covered in pale hairs that help the plants withstand cold, intense sunlight and moisture. Páramo grasses, mosses and other high-altitude species grow alongside them.

Large fields are especially striking, where the plants form an almost continuous silvery-green expanse. Scientists study local frailejón populations and their contribution to highland ecosystems. Visitors should remain on authorized paths: delicate páramo soils regenerate slowly, and trampling or removing plants compromises their protective functions.

El Ángel also contains areas of **Polylepis forest**. These Andean trees are known for their twisted trunks and distinctive bark that peels away in multiple thin layers. The woods and open frailejón fields offer two very different landscapes within the same protected area.

## El Voladero lagoons and walks in the reserve

| Area | Main feature |
|---|---|
| El Voladero lagoons | Highland water bodies and trails |
| Frailejón fields | Cold-climate páramo vegetation |
| Polylepis forest | High-altitude Andean trees |

Popular sites include the El Voladero lagoons, frailejón-covered páramo and Polylepis woods. Official tourism materials also mention other lakes and viewpoints. Ask the reserve administration which routes are authorized and which sites are accessible.

This is a conservation area. Some activities and group visits may require separate permission, and the regulations can change. Check current information before traveling rather than assuming that every trail is open to independent exploration.

Birds and other animals live here in the wild. Waterbirds and northern Andean fauna may be observed, but seeing a condor or a rare mammal is not a guaranteed part of a visit.

## Elevation and weather: what to prepare for

The reserve is in a high-mountain region, with visitor trails at approximately **3,500 meters and above**. Even relatively gentle terrain can feel more strenuous than at sea level. Weather may change quickly, with sunshine, cold wind, low clouds and rain all possible within one day.

Bring warm layers, a waterproof jacket, closed-toe shoes with good grip, water and ultraviolet protection. When planning, consider not only the trail distance but also the altitude, driving time and the participants' ability to handle physical exertion. If you have medical conditions or react badly to altitude, discuss the trip with your doctor in advance.

Wet páramo soil is not an ordinary lawn: leaving maintained paths can be dangerous and damaging to the ecosystem.

## Getting there from Quito and adding it to an itinerary

Travel to El Ángel heads north through Ecuador, generally toward Ibarra and the settlement also named El Ángel. The journey from [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/) takes a substantial part of the day, and the final sections may be on poorer road surfaces. Actual driving time depends on the chosen entrance, weather and road conditions.

On a northern Andes trip, El Ángel can be geographically combined with [Otavalo](/ecuador/place/otavalo/), [Cotacachi-Cayapas Reserve](/ecuador/place/cotacachi-cayapas/) and [Cuicocha Lake](/ecuador/place/cuicocha/). These are **separate attractions**; Cuicocha is not within El Ángel, and trying to fit every stop into one day may be too ambitious.

The northern Andes feature in the [18-day Ecuador and Galápagos tour](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/), with separate days for Otavalo and El Ángel. Another option is the [15-day Mainland Ecuador and Amazon itinerary](/ecuador/tour/mainland-ecuador-amazon-15-days/), which combines páramo with natural regions of very different climates. Consult the chosen tour description for hotels, walks and included visits.

## Conservation status and why the reserve matters

El Ángel is a protected natural area of Ecuador. In 2026, the country added the reserve to **UNESCO's World Heritage Tentative List**. Being on the Tentative List means the site has been proposed for possible future consideration; it is not the same as being inscribed on the World Heritage List.

The area's value lies in high-altitude páramo processes, local plant communities and the ability of its landscapes to retain water. Official materials report different figures for the reserve's area as boundaries and measurements have been refined. For a visit, the administration's current route maps and regulations matter more.

For travelers, El Ángel reveals a side of [Ecuador's nature](/interests/wildlife/) that is easy to miss if you focus only on the Galápagos and the Amazon: cool Andean heights, wetlands, windswept plateaus and distinctive highland vegetation.

## Frequently asked questions about El Ángel Ecological Reserve

### What is El Ángel known for?

Above all, its frailejones, high-altitude páramo, lagoons and Polylepis forests in northern Ecuador.

### Is El Ángel part of the Galápagos Islands?

No. It is in mainland Ecuador, in Carchi Province near the Colombian border.

### Can you walk through the reserve without preparation?

Some routes are suitable for ordinary walks, but the significant elevation and changeable weather require suitable clothing and an assessment of individual ability. Check access rules before departure.

### Is El Ángel already a UNESCO World Heritage Site?

No. As of 2026 it is on the Tentative List, which is different from final inscription.

## Tours through El Ángel Ecological Reserve in Ecuador

[El Ángel Ecological Reserve](/ecuador/place/el-angel-ecological-reserve/) lies in the highlands of Carchi Province in northern Ecuador. Its scenery differs dramatically from the humid Amazon rainforest and city sightseeing in Quito. Frailejones, unusual plants with dense rosettes of downy leaves, grow across the open páramo, while sheltered spots preserve Polylepis forests with characteristic layered bark.

El Ángel features in {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} offered by Ada Tours. The comparisons go beyond the reserve itself: consider the departure from the Otavalo area, a combined visit to Cuicocha Lake, time for a highland walk and subsequent travel to volcanoes or the Amazon.

Ecuador's official tourism portal gives an area of approximately 15,715 hectares for the reserve and describes high-altitude ecosystems ranging roughly from 3,644 to 4,768 meters. Even a short walk therefore calls for attention to weather, wellbeing and pace. Figures in an individual tour schedule should not be mistaken for access requirements across the entire reserve.

## Which trips include El Ángel?

| Tour | Itinerary focus |
|---|---|
| [Ecuador: Nature of the Andes and Amazon, 15 days](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-wildlife/) | Northern Andes, forests and Amazon |
| [Mainland Ecuador and Amazon, 15 days](/ecuador/tour/mainland-ecuador-amazon-15-days/) | Cuicocha, El Ángel and cloud forests |
| [Ecuador with a Galápagos cruise, 18 days](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/) | Highlands, Amazon and islands |

**The 15-day itinerary focused on nature.** On [Ecuador: Wildlife of the Andes and Amazon](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-wildlife/), El Ángel follows [Otavalo](/ecuador/place/otavalo/) and [Cotacachi-Cayapas Reserve](/ecuador/place/cotacachi-cayapas/). Day 4 involves traveling through the northern Andes, while day 5 features an excursion in the reserve. More volcanic and forest ecosystems follow, with the Amazon visited later in the trip.

**Another mainland option.** On [Ecuador and the Amazon Highlights](/ecuador/tour/mainland-ecuador-amazon-15-days/), the El Ángel visit is likewise split between the journey from [Cuicocha Lake](/ecuador/place/cuicocha/) and a separate day exploring the reserve. The itinerary includes a Polylepis forest and subsequent accommodation in the Imbabura region. It then continues through the equator line, cloud forests and other natural areas of mainland Ecuador.

**The Andes plus the Galápagos.** The [18-day itinerary](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/) features El Ángel on days 8 and 9: first travel via Otavalo and Condor Park to the Polylepis forest, then a visit to the frailejón-covered area. Later, travelers fly to the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) and spend several days aboard a yacht. This option brings high-altitude plants and the islands' marine wildlife into one journey.

## Frailejones and Polylepis forest: what you see along the route

The word *páramo* describes high-altitude grassland and shrub communities of the Andes. At El Ángel, the large frailejones are especially striking: their hairy leaves protect them in the cool, windy environment. In places, the scene resembles a multitude of silvery upright silhouettes against green slopes.

Polylepis trees grow in some sheltered hollows, with bark that peels in thin layers. Our itineraries include walks through such woodland, and some days specifically mention an evening walk by torchlight. That detail belongs to particular routes and should not be assumed to apply to every tour through the reserve.

Those who want to see mountain lakes can also visit [Cuicocha](/ecuador/place/cuicocha/), a crater lake listed separately on the northern route and usually paired with the Otavalo region. El Ángel and Cuicocha reveal different Andean environments despite their geographic proximity.

## Why the order of days matters

A visit to El Ángel generally begins after travel from lower areas of northern Ecuador. Temperature, wind and the effort of walking all change with elevation. Choose a pace that suits the group, and prepare warm outerwear and waterproof footwear. Trails and viewpoints can look very different under clouds than in sunny photographs.

When comparing the 15- and 18-day itineraries, consider how many other regions are visited after the reserve. A mainland-only route offers more opportunities to focus on the [cloud forests](/ecuador/place/bellavista-cloud-forest/) and the Amazon. Adding the Galápagos requires a flight to the archipelago and a marine program, increasing the variety of climates and transfers.

Highland nature enthusiasts can also explore [all Ecuador tours](/ecuador/tour/) and our [Nature-themed journeys](/interests/nature/). Choose according to the day-by-day itinerary rather than the number of reserve names mentioned in a title.

## Frequently asked questions about tours through El Ángel

### What is the main attraction of El Ángel?

Its distinctive frailejón-covered páramo landscapes, areas of Polylepis forest and high-altitude lakes. This is a botanical and nature experience, not a safari with guaranteed sightings of large animals.

### How does the 18-day tour differ from the 15-day tours?

After the mainland segment, the 18-day itinerary includes a flight and cruise in the Galápagos. The two 15-day trips focus on the [Andes and Amazon](/ecuador/tour/), without a cruise.

### Is the reserve suitable for relaxed walks?

The itineraries include walking sections, but the reserve itself is high in the Andes. Duration, accessible routes and participants' wellbeing should be considered individually, especially if anyone is sensitive to altitude.

### Can El Ángel be combined with Cuicocha?

Yes. Current itineraries visit [Cuicocha](/ecuador/place/cuicocha/) and El Ángel on neighboring stages of the northern Andes segment.

## El Junco Lagoon: a freshwater lake in a Galápagos volcanic crater

El Junco Lagoon lies in the green highlands of [San Cristóbal Island](/ecuador/place/san-cristobal-island/) in the [Galápagos](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). This freshwater lake fills the crater of an extinct volcano. It is strikingly different from the archipelago's coastal scenery: instead of black lava and seawater, there are moist slopes, lush vegetation and clouds that may descend all the way to the lake.

People visit for the unusual geography and birdwatching. Frigatebirds often appear overhead: these seabirds use the freshwater lagoon to bathe. Even when no birds are visible, a walk reveals an important side of San Cristóbal's nature that can easily be missed on marine excursions.

## Where El Junco is located and how to get there

The lagoon is in the interior of San Cristóbal. On the Ada Tours itinerary, the drive from Puerto Baquerizo Moreno to the El Junco area is approximately 19 km. Travelers ascend by car from the coast into a wetter part of the island and then walk to the viewing areas.

Vegetation changes with elevation: open, dry areas give way to green slopes. This makes the journey interesting even before the lake comes into view. The coastal streets may be sunny while the highlands are misty and rainy at the same time.

Galápagos National Park lists El Junco as a nature visitor site. Park staff maintain the steps and trails, as seasonal rains erode the soil and make access more difficult. Check the current condition of the paths and visitor regulations before going.

## Why the lake is freshwater

Water reaches El Junco primarily through rainfall. The volcanic basin collects it among the surrounding slopes, creating a freshwater ecosystem on an oceanic island.

This is an unusual combination. Many of the Galápagos' best-known sights are coastal: lava cliffs, sea lions, iguanas and beaches. Here, the main attraction is a water-filled volcanic crater surrounded by moister vegetation.

On a clear day, the outline of the lake is easy to make out from above. When the clouds descend, the panorama may partly disappear. This is normal highland weather, not a failure of the excursion. It is not worth crossing barriers or descending to the water along an unauthorized route just for a photograph.

## Frigatebirds and other birds at the lagoon

Frigatebirds are recognizable by their long, narrow wings and forked tails. They soar effortlessly above the sea, but El Junco attracts them because of its fresh water. Sometimes you can watch a bird circle several times before descending toward the surface.

The best approach is to stay on designated paths and observe quietly. Do not feed birds or try to lure them closer to your camera. Species diversity and bird numbers depend on the weather and natural conditions, so their presence cannot be guaranteed even during a favorable season.

The surrounding area is also interesting for its humid plant communities. Ferns and other green vegetation make this part of the island look entirely different from the dry coastal environment.

## How El Junco compares with other sites

| Place | Main attraction |
|---|---|
| El Junco | Freshwater crater lake |
| [Española](/ecuador/place/espanola-island/) | Seabirds |
| [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-highlands/) | Land tortoises |
| [San Cristóbal](/ecuador/place/san-cristobal-island/) | Volcanic island |

These places are worth comparing when choosing a route. Española is known for albatrosses, while the Santa Cruz Highlands are associated with giant tortoises. El Junco offers something different: the Galápagos' freshwater and humid habitats.

The sites are on different islands, however. Visiting them requires a coordinated vessel schedule or separate transportation; they are not connected by a short walk.

## When to visit and what to bring

The Galápagos climate varies by season, while conditions in the highlands also depend on cloud cover and altitude. Wetter periods may bring greener scenery but make paths slippery. Even in the drier season, clouds can obscure the crater.

Bring closed-toe shoes with good grip, a light waterproof jacket, drinking water and sun protection. If fog hides the view, it is better to enjoy the permitted paths and surrounding nature safely than to seek an unofficial viewpoint above the lake.

National park rules require visitors to stay on marked routes, refrain from feeding animals and keep their distance. The presence of a lake does not mean swimming is permitted.

## El Junco on an Ada Tours itinerary

The [18-day Ecuador journey with a Galápagos cruise](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/) includes a visit to El Junco on San Cristóbal. That day, you see the crater lake, have a chance to watch birds and walk in the highlands. The trip then continues as a cruise to other islands, including [Española](/ecuador/place/espanola-island/).

It illustrates how a marine itinerary can also reveal the islands' inland landscapes. Compare [wildlife and nature trips](/interests/wildlife/) with [cruises and expeditions](/interests/cruises-and-expeditions/). Always use the specific tour itinerary to determine which landings are actually planned.

## Frequently asked questions about El Junco

### Where is El Junco Lagoon?

On [San Cristóbal Island](/ecuador/place/san-cristobal-island/) in Ecuador, in the inland highlands of the Galápagos.

### Is the lake salty?

No. It is a freshwater lake fed by rainfall inside a volcanic crater.

### Are frigatebird sightings guaranteed?

No. The birds visit the lagoon, but their presence depends on natural conditions and the timing of your walk.

### Can you swim in the lagoon?

El Junco is a protected natural site regulated by the national park. Swimming should not be treated as a normal tourist activity here.

## Tour visiting El Junco Lagoon in the Galápagos

[El Junco Lagoon](/ecuador/place/el-junco-lagoon/) lies in the highlands of [San Cristóbal Island](/ecuador/place/san-cristobal-island/) in the Galápagos. The circular freshwater lake occupies the crater of an extinct volcano. Dense greenery covers the slopes, and frigatebirds can sometimes be seen over the water, visiting to bathe and groom their feathers.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} visiting the lagoon. This is the [18-day Ecuador and Galápagos itinerary](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/), combining the mainland Andes, the Amazon and a cruise through the islands. El Junco is included on the first Galápagos day. It should be understood as part of San Cristóbal's sightseeing program, not a separate multi-day tour or boat excursion.

## Which day includes the lagoon?

| Trip segment | Planned activities |
|---|---|
| Days 1–14 | Mainland Ecuador |
| Day 15 | Flight to San Cristóbal and El Junco |
| Days 16–18 | Galápagos cruise program |

After exploring highland reserves, cloud forests and the Amazon, the island section begins. Day 15 includes a flight to [San Cristóbal](/ecuador/place/san-cristobal-island/) and boarding the M/Y Grand Majestic yacht. In the afternoon, travelers head to El Junco, about 19 km from Puerto Baquerizo Moreno.

On the walk around the lagoon, you see the island's green slopes and may observe birds. This is a dry landing, and the route is of easy to moderate difficulty. The marine itinerary then continues: the following day the yacht sails to [Floreana](/ecuador/place/floreana-island/), including Post Office Bay, Punta Cormorant and [Devil's Crown](/ecuador/place/devils-crown/).

The combination is appealing because two natural environments follow one another in a short period. El Junco is a freshwater lagoon among humid slopes. The next stops involve ocean coasts, lava islands and marine wildlife.

## Why is there a freshwater lagoon in the Galápagos?

The islands are best known for their ocean, coastal cliffs and dry lava landscapes. San Cristóbal's interior slopes, however, are higher and wetter. Rainfall fills the volcanic basin at El Junco. According to Galápagos Conservancy, the lake sits approximately 700 meters above sea level and is among the archipelago's few permanent freshwater lakes.

Vegetation and rural island scenery change along the road to the lagoon. You can see the transition from drier coastal areas to humid green highlands. It is a natural experience in its own right, distinct from watching sea lions and iguanas near the ocean.

El Junco is a refuge for birds. Frigatebirds use the fresh water for bathing. Other local species occur around the lagoon too, but their presence at the moment of a visit cannot be guaranteed.

## How the walk works

Travelers reach El Junco by road from the populated part of San Cristóbal. The visit itself follows walking trails and viewpoints around the crater. The Galápagos National Park administration regularly maintains steps, barriers and boardwalks; wet ground and stairs can be slippery in rainy weather.

Comfortable closed-toe shoes, light rain protection and clothes suitable for the changing island climate are useful. Visiting the crater does not require snorkeling: this is an overland excursion. Marine activities on later days have separate rules and are subject to guides' decisions.

If San Cristóbal is your main focus, consider how much time is allocated to the island's interior. On the [18-day tour](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/), the lagoon visit takes place after the flight, on the same day as yacht embarkation. It depends on the wider schedule, so the sequence and available time must be confirmed against the final itinerary.

## Who will enjoy a route visiting El Junco?

This trip suits travelers interested in Ecuador's contrasting natural regions. The journey first explores the Andean highlands, then the humid Amazon and finally the archipelago. El Junco reveals a different side of the islands: you can walk among lush vegetation and look into a freshwater crater before the sea passages begin.

If you would rather devote the entire vacation to the Galápagos, compare this trip with the [8-day VIP cruise](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-luxury-yacht-cruise-8-days/), remembering that El Junco is not listed in its published itinerary. For a broader view, explore the [Ecuador tours catalog](/ecuador/tour/), [Nature](/interests/nature/) and [Wildlife and Safari](/interests/wildlife/) sections.

## Frequently asked questions about the tour visiting El Junco

### Which island is El Junco Lagoon on?

On [San Cristóbal](/ecuador/place/san-cristobal-island/), in the island's highlands. It is a volcanic crater filled with freshwater.

### Is the lagoon visited by boat?

No. The tour includes a land-based walk around the crater. Marine excursions begin and continue in other parts of the Galápagos itinerary.

### Can you see frigatebirds?

El Junco is known as a place where frigatebirds bathe in fresh water. Sightings depend on the timing, weather and the birds' behavior.

### Which itinerary includes El Junco?

Currently, it is the [18-day Ecuador tour with a Galápagos cruise](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/). The lagoon is scheduled for day 15, after arrival on San Cristóbal.
